Paper card. Question: Can a rocksalt high-entropy oxide containing divalent Mn and Fe be synthesized and what are its properties?. System: (Mg,Mn,Fe,Co,Ni)O. Processing: bottom-up method using oxalate precursors, annealed at 1000°C for 6 hours in argon with MnO2 as an oxygen generator. Test conditions: various temperatures and atmospheres, including air, argon, and 5% H2/Ar. Findings: FeO-HEO has a single-phase rocksalt structure; cation site occupancy is highly random; metal ions are unanimously divalent; improved structural robustness compared to constituent binary oxides; antiferromagnetic order with a magnetic transition temperature of ~218 K. Mechanism: the oxygen sublattice acts as a buffer layer to accommodate different metal ions, and the cocktail effect contributes to the improved phase stability. Future work: dedicated study to determine the magnetic structure and correlations, and assessment of whether iron carries an orbital magnetic moment in this FeO-HEO. Quote: "a generic method was developed to synthesize rocksalt high-entropy oxides containing divalent manganese and iron"

Mechanism: The authors propose that the machine learning models can learn the complex relationships between the features and the phases of HEAs, allowing for accurate predictions. Limitations: The dataset is imbalanced, with some phase categories having more records than others. Paper card. Question: How does ultrafine-grain microstructure affect the oxidation behavior of AlCoCrFeNi high entropy alloy?. System: AlCoCrFeNi high entropy alloy. Processing: Stationary friction processing (SFP) at 400 and 1800 rpm for 5 min. Test conditions: Oxidation at 850-1050 °C for 100 h in laboratory air. Findings: Ultrafine-grain microstructure reduces oxidation kinetics by 12-48%; Parabolic rate constant is lower for ultrafine-grained samples; Activation energy for oxidation is higher for ultrafine-grained samples; Protective oxide scales of Al2O3 and Cr2O3 form on ultrafine-grained samples; Internal oxidation zone (IOZ) forms in ultrafine-grained samples. Mechanism: The enhanced oxidation resistance of ultrafine-grained samples is attributed to the formation of a dense protective Cr2O3 layer followed by internal Al-rich oxide layered structure, which acts as a barrier for the oxidation process. Quote: "The ultrafine-grained samples showed a phase transition from BCC/B2 to FCC structure"

Paper card. Question: Can a phase prediction method for high-entropy alloys (HEAs) be developed by integrating a criterion and machine learning recommendation method?. System: High-entropy alloys (HEAs). Findings: The proposed phase prediction of HEAs (PPH) achieves an average prediction accuracy of 91.6% in all HEAs.; The PPH achieves an average prediction accuracy of 94.3% in quinary HEAs.; The PPH achieves an average prediction accuracy of 93.1% in senary HEAs.; The PPH achieves an average prediction accuracy of 95.8% in septenary HEAs.. Mechanism: The PPH combines the advantages of the criterion of SS and MLRM, where the criterion of SS has strong interpretability and generalization and requires only a small amount of training samples.. Limitations: The performance of the meta-learner in traditional meta-learning is not ideal, and the KNN does not fully consider the information of the left and right nearest neighbors of every sample.. Future work: The PPH can also provide a research foundation in other material fields.. Quote: "The comprehensive properties of high-entropy alloys (HEAs) are highly-dependent on their phases."

System: Co35Cr25Ni15Mn15Fe10 (at%) high-entropy alloy.
